name: Tim Scott

issue_poll.name: South Carolina Policy Council voter poll (Spry Strategies), May 31–Jun 3, 2022; Pew Research Center national survey, Oct 10–16, 2022
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–5 from the SCPC most-important-issue question (inflation 26%, energy independence 24%, drug addiction/mental illness/homelessness 13%, border security 12%, election security 10%); SCPC published only those five. Ranks 6–10 from Pew's national 'very important' list, skipping items already covered and 'future of democracy': education 64%, health care 63%, violent crime 61%, gun policy 57%, abortion 56% (https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2022/10/PP_2022.10.20_midterms-economy_REPORT.pdf). No fall 2022 SC poll with an issue ranking was found.

issues.position: Block IRA funding for added IRS agents
issues.note: Both bills cut IRA IRS funding. He opposed the debt-limit bill, calling it a blank check (https://www.scott.senate.gov/media-center/press-releases/senator-scott-opposes-giving-biden-administration-blank-check/).

issues.position: Revive Keystone XL; resume oil and gas leasing on public lands
issues.note: H.R.1 required onshore and offshore oil and gas lease sales; Keystone XL got no vote. Also https://www.foxnews.com/media/gas-tax-holiday-tricks-market-domestic-speculation-easier-fix-tim-scott
His FEND Off Fentanyl Act push dates from 2023, after the campaign.
Title 42 and border-wall pledges found date from his 2023 presidential run, not the Senate campaign.

issues.position: Criticized Democrats' 2022 voting bills; no forward plan stated
Bar student loan cancellation; expand school choice

votes.bill_title: Disapproval of student loan debt relief rule
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: School choice is from his 2022 campaign letter (https://www.democracyinaction.us/lit/22sen/scsen22r.html); H.R.1 created a permanent school-choice tax credit. Loan vote confirmed by his release (https://www.scott.senate.gov/media-center/press-releases/senator-scott-fights-back-against-biden-administrations-illegal-and-unfair-student-loan-cancellation-policy-protects-working-americans).

issues.position: Blamed Democrats for more crime; no specific policy
Oppose gun laws that infringe Second Amendment rights

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: Failed 49-44; Collins and Murkowski were the only Republican yes votes and Scott (SC) was not absent (https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/wednesday-july-10-2024).

caveats: SCPC poll is from June 2022 and published only five issues; ranks 6–10 rely on national Pew data.
No 2022 campaign issues page, debate, or questionnaire found (votetimscott.com archive not reachable); positions come from campaign literature, ads, interviews and 2022 Senate releases.
Inflation scored Mixed: the Fiscal Responsibility Act he opposed also cut IRS funding, though it was mainly a debt-limit bill.
Roll call numbers 146, 135, 171, 211 and 372 come from other researched files and third-party trackers; his S.4554 Nay is inferred from the tally and absentee list.
